body:
📊 *weekly triage digest* — 2026-07-17 → 2026-07-24

⚠ *Window note:* the routine was dark for 6 of these 7 days (2026-07-17 → 2026-07-22, zero poll-cycles in the incident log) — the tail of the already-diagnosed 8-day laptop-hibernation gap (2026-07-15 17:08Z → 2026-07-23 20:11Z). It resumed with one large backlog catch-up (45 groups) plus two quiet cycles, all on 2026-07-23. Every number below is real, but it's the shape of a single burst-day, not 7 days of organic cadence — treat week-over-week deltas as not meaningful this cycle.

*Volume:* 48 alerts triaged · 27 posted · 4 suppressed to digest (+ 17 false-alarm self-DM confirmations, counted separately — no post, no digest entry)

*Top recurrences this week*
| occ | entry | fix_status |
|-----|-------|------------|
| 2 | ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring | investigating |
| 1 each | 24 other KB entries (ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout, ki-2026-07-03-method-ui-grid-dropdown-performance-test-nodata, ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap, +21 more) | mixed |

*New this week:* none (no KB entries with first_seen in this window)
*Aging:* oldest unchanged fix_status — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout` still `chronic-residual-post-rollback-2026-06-05` (48d unchanged, 580 occurrences all-time, #1 by volume). Broader aging audit is limited — the KB doesn't track a status-change timestamp separately from the status string itself.
*Concentration:* top 3 = 4 of this week's 26 KIR occurrences (~15%) — unusually flat vs the standing ~64% top-3-of-all-time figure, because the catch-up burst logged most chronic entries exactly once instead of at their normal hourly cadence. Not a real de-concentration trend.
*Suppression ratio:* 4/48 (~8%) suppressed to digest this week — unusually low. The single mega-cycle's 24h KIR window had expired for almost every chronic entry simultaneously (last touched before the gap), so nearly everything resurfaced as a post instead of being suppressed.

One thing worth doing next week: confirm the hibernation-gap fix (watchdog / wake scheduling) actually holds — this is the second consecutive digest window disrupted by it.

[known issue recurrence] `ki-2026-07-05-rainforest-outbound-api-p95-latency`
This is occurrence #10 in the last 7 days (every-10th-occurrence resurface rule).
Owning team (would tag - not tagged): `Transactions` (`@transactions` / `#team-transactions`)
Playbook: third-party (Rainforest) API latency blip, self-recovering, no Method-side fix. Escalate only if frequency/errors increase.
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total):
  - n/a - degraded cycle, no Slack MCP read path this session (no permalink available). DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295928665

Evidence:
  - DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295928665 - "[Rainforest] Outbound API P95 Latency > 3s" (OK, self-recovered)
  - DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.http.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cpeer.hostname%3Aapi.rainforestpay.com&exp_agg=p95&start=1784847145&end=1784854345 - 23 datapoints, max ~0.5s, well under the 3s threshold
  - DD logs: service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod, 2026-07-23T22:52:25Z-2026-07-24T00:52:25Z - 0 hits
  - This-window concentration: n/a - third-party latency-only signal, no service-side error breakdown available

[known issue recurrence - escalated per KB playbook] `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
Occurrence #11. Normally suppressed (inside the 24h window), but escalating because this occurrence breaks the KB's own documented "cleanest non-reproduction pattern": a single p95 datapoint of 55849.8s (~15.5h) at 08:30:00Z, vs. a pristine ~0.001-0.05s baseline before/after. Per the KB's own playbook step 4: "if a 3rd occurrence ever shows a genuine elevated p95, treat as a break from this pattern and escalate immediately."
Owning team (would tag - not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@crm-experience` / `#team-crm-experience` - not independently confirmed against ownership.md's Teams table this cycle, rendered inert regardless)

Working hypothesis (UNCONFIRMED): notifications runs SignalR Hub connections; if trace.aspnet.request instrumentation records "request duration" only when a long-lived WebSocket connection finally closes, a Hub connection open ~15.5h would produce exactly this single-bucket outlier shape as an APM artifact, not a real latency regression. Consistent with 0 error-level logs and a pristine surrounding baseline. NOT yet confirmed with the owning team.

Source alerts (1 total):
  - n/a - degraded cycle, no Slack MCP read path this session (no permalink available). DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327

Evidence:
  - DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327 - "[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high"
  - DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Anotifications&exp_agg=p95&start=1784881387&end=1784883187 - single 55849.8s outlier at 08:30:00Z, all other 179 points 0.001-0.05s
  - DD logs: service:notifications status:error env:prod, same window - 0 hits
  - This-window concentration: n/a - also newly observed (chronic, not new-today): ~45k/24h "Hub Connection MethodAuth Validation Warning" (AccessTokenNotFound) logs across many accounts, comparable to ~60k/24h the prior day - not mechanistically tied to this specific outlier bucket
  - Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-07-24-838378d61cf54ca5.md
